units.translation: πληθύεται Μ [it is increased, M]. i.e. in which direction the will of the people inclines more, or, as the scholiast says, πότερον πλείους οἱ συμμαχοῦντες ἡμῖν ἢ ὀλίγοι [whether those fighting on our side are more or fewer]. Similarly
where the persons of the chorus state their opinion individually, the one who speaks last says ταύτην (τὴν γνώμην) [this (opinion)], he says, ἐπαινεῖν πάντοθεν [to praise from all sides]
the hand of the people prevailing, wherever
whether those fighting on our side are more or fewer
Πλήθουσι νε-κρῶν δυσπότμως ἐφθαρμένων [they are full of corpses destroyed by an evil fate]
Θάλασσα δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἦν ἰδεῖν ναυαγίων [and the sea was no longer to be seen because of the shipwrecks]
[Πλάθουσι [they are full] was wrongly accepted by some for πλήθουσι [they are full], about which I have spoken under πλάθω]
being full also of the slaughter of mortals
being full of their own food
they are full of corpses destroyed by an evil fate
and the sea was no longer to be seen because of the shipwrecks
Σταγόνες ἄφαρκτοι δυσχίμου [unfenced drops of stormy weather]
Συλλαβα μεδια βρεβις εστ apud Ομηρ, λογα apud τραγικος, ανεψ apud Απολλονιος Ροδιος. [The middle syllable is short in Homer, long in the tragedians, and anceps in Apollonius Rhodius.]
Οὐκ ἄλλο γ᾽ οὐδὲν [nothing else at all]
Τί γὰρ πέπρωται Ζηνὶ [for what is fated for Zeus]
Τί σοι πέπρακται πρᾶγμα [what deed has been done by you]
Τὸ δ᾽ ἄρσεν αἰνῶ πάντα [and I praise the male in all things]
Ἐλεύθερος γὰρ οὔτις ἐστὶ [for no one is free]
Καὶ τοῖσιν οὐδεὶς ἀντέβαινε [and no one opposed them]
Οὐδεὶς θεῶν δύναιτ᾽ ἂν αὐτῷ [none of the gods could against him]
Οὐκ ἔχω προσ-εικάσαι πάντ᾽ ἐπισταθμώμενος [I cannot liken it, weighing all things]
Οὐκ ἔστιν ὅστις [there is no one who]
except to rule over the gods
except when it seems good to him
except if I am released from bonds
no one could justly blame me for this
except the gods, all things unharmed for all time?
except the nature of the earth that nourishes Helios
for what is fated for Zeus
what deed has been done by you
and I praise the male in all things
none of the gods could against him
I cannot liken it, weighing all things
Φιμοὶ δὲ συρίζουσι βάρβαρον νόμον, μυκτηροκόμποις πνεύμασιν [and the muzzles whistle a barbarian tune, with nostril-boasting breaths]
Τοιοίδε τοί μοι λαμπαδηφόρων νόμοι, ἄλλος παρ᾽ ἄλλου διαδοχαῖς [such are the laws of the torch-bearers for me, one from another in succession]
Τῷ δ᾽ ἐναντίῳ κύτει Ἐλπὶς προσήει χειρὸς οὐ [and to the opposite vessel Hope approached, not of the hand]
Σάλπιγξ βροτείου πνεύματος [trumpet of mortal breath]
Πληρουμένου γὰρ τοῦδε [for when this is being filled]
Ἀἴγυπτος ἁγνοῦ νάματος [Egypt of pure stream]
and the muzzles whistle a barbarian tune, with nostril-boasting breaths
such are the laws of the torch-bearers for me, one from another in succession
and to the opposite vessel Hope approached, not of the hand
